protocol.instrument_name: Northern Territory Community Pharmacy Full Scope of Practice Program - Service Provision Rules
protocol.instrument_version: 1.0 (version table prints '1.0 | 15/05/2026 | Medicines and Poisons | First Version'; page footer prints '15 May 2026 | Version 1')
protocol.legal_basis: Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 2012 (NT) and Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulations 2014 (NT). 'In May 2026, the Northern Territory Government amended the Regulations to provide appropriately trained pharmacists be included in the relevant sections of the Act which enable, and regulate, the supply and use of prescriptions for Schedule 4 and 8 medicines.' Legislation adopts the national Poisons Standard (p.4, 1. Introduction). 'Non-adherence to this framework may be a breach of legislation and/or professional standards and behaviour.' (p.5).
protocol.supervision_model: Authorisation under the Regulation with self-managed professional autonomy, document terminology: 'NT Health takes a principles and outcomes based regulatory approach that recognises the level of autonomy of professional practice required by health practitioners' (p.4); pharmacists are 'authorised under the new Regulation' (p.4) and 'are not required to obtain direct approval from the Chief Health Officer or NT Health prior to participation, however there are several critical requirements which require engagement with NT Health prior to being able to deliver services' (p.7); registration with the Chief Pharmacist is required prior to commencing practice and 'no longer than 72 hours of providing the expanded clinical services in the NT' (p.8).
protocol.scope_summary: FRAMEWORK DOCUMENT (program service rules, not a condition-specific treatment protocol). Sets the scope of practices permitted under the NT Community Pharmacy Full Scope of Practice Program (Appendix A substance/indication/restriction table), pharmacist and pharmacy eligibility requirements, consent and fee duties, professional communication and clinical record-keeping duties, pathology/testing limitations, applicable guidelines, fees, incident/feedback management and related documents. It contains no dosing schedules; condition-level clinical protocols are separate documents. Approved by Chief Pharmacist 15/05/2026, review annually (p.2).

inclusion.text: Pharmacists must have completed a program of training that is the Australia Qualifications Framework Level 8 that is accredited by the Tertiary Education Quality Standards Agency or the Australian Skills Authority and provides skills in: Prescribing Competency - information gathering, clinical and shared decision making, communication and evaluation which results in the initiation, continuation or cessation of a medicine and; Clinical Competency - epidemiology, anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology and specific skills in clinical assessment, diagnosis, therapeutic and non-therapeutic management for conditions permitted under these rules.
The course must be accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council
The pharmacist must hold general registration with the Pharmacy Board of Australia with no conditions or notations that affect the delivery of clinical services.
Pharmacist must hold professional indemnity insurance that explicitly covers the activities being conducted by the pharmacist
Register with the Chief Pharmacist prior to commencing practice in the NT and no longer than 72 hours of providing the expanded clinical services in the NT
Follow relevant NT and national Guidelines on conditions being managed.
Must only provide clinical services when the patient themselves is attending the pharmacy

Provide advice on the financial cost of the service prior to gaining patient consent to receive the service. This must include advice on the availability of no-cost services the patient can reasonably access based on their location.

Gain active consent from the patient to participate in the service which includes a notice that the consultation may not result in a medication being provided, as well as the potential for referral if the condition is not within the pharmacists scope of practice.

Pharmacists may only practice in a Pharmacy Business (as defined in the Health Practitioners Act 2004) which meets the following requirements: The Pharmacy Premises must meet any specific Standards set by the Pharmacy Premises Committee; The Pharmacy has an appropriate Clinical Information System to record the service provision; The Pharmacy has a dedicated consultation room for clinical services

For Medicines Management Services: The Pharmacist must advise the patient on the impact of the Management Service on PBS benefits and continuity of care required with their regular provider; Maintain appropriate records of the Management Service provided including but not limited to appropriate annotation of the prescription.

Pharmacies where clinical services are being delivered must have Mandatory Equipment: The room must contain an examination table, or all-purpose fully reclinable bed chair that is suitable for patient examinations and procedures; Disposal bins for sharps or other consumables as well as appropriate clinical waste management processes; Access to a height management device; Access to a scale or weighing machine; A first aid kit; An anaphylaxis management kit; Appropriate diagnostic equipment for services provided, such as Blood pressure monitoring, Otoscope, Pulse Oximeter Monitor. Where a single pharmacist is on duty, the pharmacy must have appropriate processes to guarantee that the pharmacist can provide uninterrupted care to an individual patient.

Expanded services must be conducted in a screened area or room separate from the public. The area must: (PS5) be of sufficient area to accommodate the consumer, their carer and the pharmacist, at least 7m2; allow sufficient space, surfaces and equipment to respond to medical emergencies including sufficient space for the consumer to lie down and for the pharmacist to manoeuvre around the consumer; provide seating, appropriately placed to adhere to social distancing requirements; ensure the privacy of the consumer such that the consultation is not visible or audible to other persons; contain a bench or table of at least 0.6m2; (PS2) The room must be compliant with all relevant Australian Standards including AS 1428.1 Design for access and mobility; Sufficient lighting for 'routine office tasks' eg: reading, writing and typing having an illumination range of 320-400 Lux. - AS/NZS 1680.1 Interior workplace lighting; Easy access to a sink with running water for washing hands and ready access to hand sanitiser; Electronic equipment to allow practitioner access to: Clinical information and Patient management/documentation system

The program enables 'Enhanced acute treatment/management of conditions including:' Acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis (Patients aged 18 years or over); Acute minor wound management (Patients aged 5 years or over); Acute nausea and vomiting (Patients aged 18 years or over); Allergic and nonallergic rhinitis (hay fever); Ear infections; Reflux; Shingles; Initiation of Hormonal Contraceptives; Impetigo (school sores); Management for overweight and obesity; Mild to moderate acne; Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; Mild, acute, musculoskeletal pain; Oral health risk assessment and fluoride application; Smoking cessation; Travel health - acute mountain sickness, traveller's diarrhoea, malaria prophylaxis. 'As outlined in Appendix A of this document.'
Amendment of existing prescriptions for dose/form to permit continuity of care
Supply of, or issuing of a prescription for, Schedule 4 medicines within scope of practice, training and capacity to provide an enhanced clinical service.
Adjustment of medicine and/or dose, including deprescribing, to best manage therapeutic effect and dose related adverse effects
Management/support for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction, Asthma and/or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.

Acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis - Substance: A topical medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Dermatology: Psoriasis'. Restriction: For persons aged 16 years or over.

Acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomitting: Antiemetic drugs in adults'. Restriction: For non-pregnant persons aged 18 years or over.

Acute minor wound management - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Antibiotic: Traumatic wound infections: Bite wound infections, including clench-first injury infections; or 'Antibiotic: Traumatic wound infections: Traumatic wound infections; or 'Antibiotic: Traumatic wound infections: Water-immersed wound infections'. Restriction: For persons aged 5 years or over.

Acute minor wound management - Substance: Lidocaine preparations of 1% or less in accordance with the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Pain and analgesia: Drugs used for pain: Local anaesthetics for acute pain management'. Restriction: For persons aged 5 years or over.

Acute otitis media - treatment and/or management of associated pain - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Pain and Analgesia: Pharmacological management of acute pain: Mild, acute nociceptive pain'; or 'Antibiotic: Ear, nose and thoat infections: Otitis media'. Restriction: For persons aged 2 years or over.

Allergic and nonallergic rhinitis - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Respiratory: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis: Allergic rhinitis; or 'Respiratory: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis: Nonallergic rhinitis'. Restriction: Excluding ocular medicines containing ketorolac or corticosteroids. (No age restriction printed in this row.)

Gastro-oesophageal reflux and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Gastrointestinal: Oesophageal disorders: Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults'. Restriction: For persons aged 18 years to 55 years.

Impetigo - Substance: A topical or oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Antibiotic: Skin and soft tissue infections: Impetigo'. Restriction: For persons aged 1 year or over.

Management for overweight and obesity - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Cardiovascular: Modifiable lifestyle risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: Excess body weight, obesity and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk'. Restriction: For persons aged 18 years or over. Excluding liraglutide, semaglutide and naltrexone + bupropion.

Mild to moderate acne - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Dermatology: Acne'. Restriction: For persons aged 12 years or over.

Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis - Substance: A topical medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Dermatology: Dermatitis: Atopic dermatitis'. Restriction: For persons aged 6 months or over.

Mild, acute, musculoskeletal pain - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Pain and Analgesia: Pharmacological management of acute pain: Mild, acute nociceptive pain'; or 'Rheumatology: Overview of limb conditions: Analgesia for acute soft-tissue limb conditions'. Restriction: For persons aged 18 years or over.

Shingles - treatment and/or management of associated pain - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Pain and analgesia: Pharmacological management of acute pain: Mild, acute nociceptive pain'; or 'Pain and Analgesia: Managing specific pain syndromes: Pain associated with shingles (herpes zoster): Acute pain associated with shingles (herpes zoster)'; or 'Antibiotic: Skin and soft tissue infections: Shingles (herpes zoster)'. Restriction: For persons aged 18 years or over.

Treatment of nicotine dependence - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Addiction: Tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence'. Restriction: For persons aged 18 years or over. Excluding nortriptyline and nicotine vaping products.

Travel health - Acute mountain sickness - standby treatment and/or standby management of associated symptoms - Substance: An oral medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Wilderness medicine: Altitude illness'; or 'Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomiting'. Restriction: For persons aged 8 years or over.

Travel health - Travellers' diarhoea - standby emergency treatment and/or standby management of associated symptoms - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the sections of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled: 'Antibiotic: Infectious diarrhoea: Travellers' diarrhoea'; or 'Gastrointestinal: Acute gastroenteritis: Other supportive therapy and considerations for acute gastroenteritis: Antidiarroheal drugs for acute gastroenteritis'. Restriction: For persons aged 2 years or over.

Travel health - Malaria - prophylaxis or standby emergency treatment of uncomplicated malaria - Substance: A medicine mentioned in the current online version of the section of the Therapeutic Guidelines titled 'Antibiotic: Parasitic infections: Malaria'. Restriction: For persons aged 8 years or over.

Contraception - Substance: Combined hormonal contraception - combined oral contraceptives (COCs) and the contraceptive vaginal ring. Restriction: Excluding preparations containing 50 micrograms or more of ethinylestradiol, or preparations containing mestranol. (No age restriction printed in this row.)
Contraception - Substance: Progesterone-only contraceptive pill. Restriction column in the extracted text reads 'Contraception' (misaligned); no age restriction can be read for this row.
Contraception - Substance: Depot medroxyprogesterone (injection). Restriction column in the extracted text reads 'Contraception' (misaligned); no age restriction can be read for this row.

exclusion.text: Pharmacists are not permitted to prescribe or otherwise deal with Schedule 8 medicines under this program.
Pharmacists are not permitted to prescribe or otherwise deal with any Monitored Medicine under this program
Allergic and nonallergic rhinitis: Excluding ocular medicines containing ketorolac or corticosteroids.
Management for overweight and obesity: Excluding liraglutide, semaglutide and naltrexone + bupropion.
Treatment of nicotine dependence: Excluding nortriptyline and nicotine vaping products.

Contraception (combined hormonal contraception - COCs and the contraceptive vaginal ring): Excluding preparations containing 50 micrograms or more of ethinylestradiol, or preparations containing mestranol.

NT Health Infectious Disease units recommend: avoiding the use of antibiotics, including topical Mupirocin, for treatment of Impetigo and prioritising non-antibiotic options for treatment of Otitis Media/Externa under this program. (Printed as a recommendation, not as a prohibition; recorded here because it restricts antibiotic use under the program.)

exclusion_exceptions.text: Pharmacists participating in this program may continue to use existing rights on supply from verbal order or emergency supply privileges for these medicines. (Exception to the Schedule 8 / Monitored Medicine prohibition in 4.2 Controlled Medicine use.)

steps.description: 'Before initiating a Schedule 4 medicine to a person, the pharmacist must undertake an individualised clinical assessment of the person's health needs, including relevant medical history, symptoms and investigations as part of the consultation to determine suitability for any prescribed treatment.'

gates.criterion: Individualised clinical assessment of the person's health needs (relevant medical history, symptoms and investigations) undertaken before initiating a Schedule 4 medicine

steps.description: Confirm the person's condition, the substance class and the person's age fall within a row of Appendix A (Substance / Indication / Restrictions), pp.13-15. Consent must include a notice of 'the potential for referral if the condition is not within the pharmacists scope of practice' (p.8, 5.2. Participation requirements).

gates.criterion: Condition, substance and patient age fall within an Appendix A row (Substance/Indication/Restrictions)

steps.description: For Impetigo and Otitis Media/Externa apply the printed NT Health Infectious Disease units recommendations: 'avoiding the use of antibiotics, including topical Mupirocin, for treatment of Impetigo and' 'prioritising non-antibiotic options for treatment of Otitis Media/Externa under this program.'

gates.criterion: For Impetigo or Otitis Media/Externa, non-antibiotic options are prioritised per NT Health Infectious Disease units recommendation

steps.description: 'Where managing any condition that pathology is required or best practice, pharmacists must assess the potential impact of patient access to testing.' Pharmacists are 'currently not recognised under the Health Insurance Act to request pathology testing that is government subsidised. As such, patients referred for laboratory testing may face difficulties in accessing this.'

gates.criterion: Potential impact of patient access to pathology/laboratory testing assessed where pathology is required or best practice

steps.description: Before the service: 'Provide advice on the financial cost of the service prior to gaining patient consent to receive the service. This must include advice on the availability of no-cost services the patient can reasonably access based on their location.' and 'Gain active consent from the patient to participate in the service which includes a notice that the consultation may not result in a medication being provided, as well as the potential for referral if the condition is not within the pharmacists scope of practice.'

gates.criterion: Financial cost advice given and active consent obtained (including notice that the consultation may not result in a medication being provided and possible referral if out of scope)

steps.description: 'Supply of, or issuing of a prescription for, Schedule 4 medicines within scope of practice, training and capacity to provide an enhanced clinical service.' 'Schedule 4 medicines supplied/prescribed under this program are not eligible for PBS subsidisation and the costs of medicines must be explained to patients and alternative options provided where cost of the medicine is a barrier.' No doses are printed in this framework document.

gates.criterion: Costs of the Schedule 4 medicine explained to the patient and alternative options provided where cost of the medicine is a barrier

steps.description: 'make and keep (at the pharmacy where the person's consultation occurred) a comprehensive clinical record of the consultation and of any prescriptions given to a person, in accordance with relevant legislation and professional responsibilities.' Record must include (a)-(g): identification of the person; name of the pharmacist and their healthcare identifier number (HPI-I); date of the consultation; information relevant to the person's diagnosis and treatment; any clinical opinion reached and actions taken; details of the management plan (prescriptions with generic name, form, strength, quantity, instructions for use; advice on proposed treatment; advice about recommended follow up); any consent given.

gates.criterion: Comprehensive clinical record made and kept at the pharmacy where the consultation occurred, containing items (a) to (g)

steps.description: 'The pharmacist must offer a record of the consultation to the person, including details of any changes to their medication management.'

gates.criterion: Record of the consultation offered to the person, including details of any changes to their medication management

steps.description: 'Following consent, the pharmacist should share a record of the consultation via secure transfer to the person's usual treating healthcare practitioner or medical practice, where the person has one and upload to the patients My Health Record.'

gates.criterion: Consent obtained to share the consultation record

steps.description: 'For medication management and continuation of care services - intent is to resolve the patients' current access to appropriate medicines issue and then return their care to their primary provider for appropriate review and re-issuing of prescriptions as needed. This advice must be provided to the patient when performing this service.'

gates.criterion: Patient advised that care will be returned to their primary provider for appropriate review and re-issuing of prescriptions as needed

open_questions.topic: Psoriasis age contradiction between scope list and Appendix A
open_questions.observed: Page 6 (4. Scope of practices permitted) prints 'Acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis (Patients aged 18 years or over)'; Appendix A on page 13 prints 'For persons aged 16 years or over.' for the same indication.
open_questions.why_unclear: Two different printed age thresholds for the same indication; not reconciled - both readings recorded (INC-14 uses the p.6 wording, INC-19 uses the p.13 wording).

open_questions.observed: The document prints 'must' requirements for pharmacists/pharmacies (pp.7-10), a scope list (pp.5-6) and an Appendix A table of alternatives (pp.13-15), but never states all_of/any_of semantics.
open_questions.why_unclear: Combinators inferred: participation requirements all_of (INC-1..INC-13), scope statements all_of (INC-14..INC-18), Appendix A rows any_of (a patient presents with one qualifying substance/indication/restriction). The relationship BETWEEN these groups is not printed; document does not state that a patient must satisfy one row from each group.

open_questions.topic: Appendix A table extraction is imperfect
open_questions.observed: The Substance/Indication/Restrictions table spans pp.13-15 and the extracted text interleaves cells (e.g. the shingles row runs across pp.14-15; the contraception rows on p.15 show the Restrictions column reading 'Contraception').
open_questions.why_unclear: Table rows may be misaligned; Appendix A rows carry confidence medium, and the progesterone-only pill and depot medroxyprogesterone rows carry confidence unclear (INC-37, INC-38).

open_questions.topic: Scope list item without an Appendix A row
open_questions.observed: 'Oral health risk assessment and fluoride application' is listed in the permitted conditions on p.6, but no corresponding row appears in Appendix A (pp.13-15).
open_questions.why_unclear: Authorised substances, indication wording and age restriction for oral health are not printed in this document.

open_questions.topic: Scope list wording differs from Appendix A wording
open_questions.observed: Page 6 lists 'Ear infections', 'Reflux' and 'Smoking cessation' whereas Appendix A specifies 'Acute otitis media - treatment and/or management of associated pain' (2 years or over), 'Gastro-oesophageal reflux and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease' (18 to 55 years) and 'Treatment of nicotine dependence' (18 years or over).
open_questions.why_unclear: Whether the p.6 general terms are limited to the Appendix A rows (and their age bands) is not stated.

open_questions.observed: No single program-wide age limit is printed. Per-indication restrictions range from 'For persons aged 6 months or over' (mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, p.14) to 'For persons aged 18 years to 55 years' (gastro-oesophageal reflux, p.14).
open_questions.why_unclear: min_years 0.5 is derived from the youngest printed band (6 months, p.14); max_years left null because the 55-year upper bound applies only to the gastro-oesophageal reflux row, not the program.

open_questions.topic: Referral block provenance span and empty emergency list
open_questions.observed: Referral duties appear on pp.8 (scope referral notice), p.9 (return care to primary provider) and p.10 (secure transfer to usual treating practitioner). No emergency referral destination, timeframe or escalation number is printed anywhere in the document.
open_questions.why_unclear: Shared referral provenance uses the first page (8); the emergency list is empty because the document genuinely prints none. Closest emergency content is a premises requirement ('space, surfaces and equipment to respond to medical emergencies', p.9), which is not a referral destination.

open_questions.observed: The antimicrobial-stewardship duty (4.1. Antibiotic use, p.7) and the pathology access duty (8. Pathology and Testing, p.10) are stated as duties/recommendations with no branching instruction.
open_questions.why_unclear: No follow-on action is printed when the duty is not met, so gates PW-1-S3 and PW-1-S4 use on_fail 'unclear'.

open_questions.topic: Contraception rows carry no age restriction
open_questions.observed: Appendix A p.15 contraception rows print substance restrictions (e.g. excluding preparations containing 50 micrograms or more of ethinylestradiol) but no age, and p.6 'Initiation of Hormonal Contraceptives' prints no age either.
open_questions.why_unclear: No numeric age bound is printed for contraception; cannot be inferred from other rows.

open_questions.topic: Section heading mismatch in contents vs body
open_questions.observed: Contents (p.3) lists '11. Incident reporting'; the printed heading on p.11 reads '11. Incidents and feedback'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Minor numbering/wording inconsistency in the source; provenance uses the heading as printed on the page where content appears.

open_questions.observed: The document does not print any notifiable-condition reporting duty. It does require, following consent, sharing the consultation record with the person's usual treating healthcare practitioner/medical practice and uploading to My Health Record (p.10).
open_questions.why_unclear: required set to true for those notification/sharing duties only, and both are conditional on consent; no notifiable condition list exists in this document.

open_questions.topic: Incident and feedback processes not specified
open_questions.observed: Pharmacies 'must have appropriate policies for recording, management and reporting of incidents involving medicines' (QSPP requirements) and should have processes for consumer feedback and understand the role of the Health Practitioner Complaints Commissioner and Open Disclosure (pp.11-12).
open_questions.why_unclear: No specific reporting pathway, timeframe or recipient is printed, so it is not structured as a red flag; it is flagged for local policy confirmation instead.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Correct age for 'Acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis': p.6 states 'Patients aged 18 years or over' while Appendix A p.13 states 'For persons aged 16 years or over'. Confirm the authoritative age with NT Health before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Direct contradiction between two printed age thresholds for the same indication; both readings recorded, not reconciled.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm which substance/indication row authorises 'Oral health risk assessment and fluoride application' (listed in scope on p.6 but absent from Appendix A pp.13-15), including any age restriction.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Scope lists a service that has no Appendix A substance definition; authorised substances are therefore unknown.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how to apply the NT Health Infectious Disease units recommendations (avoid antibiotics including topical Mupirocin for Impetigo; prioritise non-antibiotic options for Otitis Media/Externa, p.7) alongside Appendix A rows that expressly authorise antibiotic medicines for Impetigo and Otitis media.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Recommendation and authorised-substance table pull in opposite directions; the document does not state which governs at the point of supply.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm whether the p.6 term 'Ear infections' is limited to the Appendix A 'Acute otitis media' row (aged 2 years or over) or also covers otitis externa, which appears only in the 4.1 antibiotic recommendation.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Scope wording and Appendix A wording differ; eligibility boundary for non-otitis-media ear conditions is not printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the specific AQF Level 8, TEQSA/ASA-accredited and Australian Pharmacy Council-accredited training course that satisfies the pharmacist training requirement before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The requirement is printed but no approved course list is provided in this document.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the exact NT Health engagements required despite 'not required to obtain direct approval from the Chief Health Officer or NT Health prior to participation, however there are several critical requirements which require engagement with NT Health' (p.7), including the Chief Pharmacist registration process and the 72-hour timeframe on p.8.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document hedges on which engagements are mandatory and how registration must be completed; local process is not printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm fee disclosure arrangements and the approach to non-PBS supply: 'Schedule 4 medicines supplied/prescribed under this program are not eligible for PBS subsidisation and the costs of medicines must be explained to patients and alternative options provided where cost of the medicine is a barrier' (p.11); fees are otherwise left to the pharmacist/pharmacy.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Fee levels and cost-disclosure process are left to local policy; PBS claiming is out of scope for this extraction (OpenScript D-001).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local incident-reporting, consumer-feedback and Open Disclosure processes under the Quality and Safety Pharmacy Program, and the escalation route to the Health Practitioner Complaints Commissioner (pp.11-12).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document requires policies but prints no specific process, timeframe or recipient; must be confirmed against local SOPs before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pin the versions of 'the current online version' of Therapeutic Guidelines sections (and the QLD/SA guideline sets) that define every Appendix A authorised substance, since Appendix A defers to the live online versions.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Authorised substance sets are version-dependent and change over time; the document prints no version or date.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the age boundaries for the progesterone-only contraceptive pill and depot medroxyprogesterone (injection) rows of Appendix A, where the extracted restriction column reads 'Contraception' (misaligned).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Table row appears misaligned in text extraction; no age printed that can be attributed with confidence.
